:::{#def-right-hand-derivative}
#### Right-hand derivative

Let $f$ be a function defined at $c$.
The **right-hand derivative** of $f$ at $c$ is the right-hand limit (@def-right-hand-limit)
$\lim_{h \to 0^+} \frac{f(c + h) - f(c)}{h}$ of the difference quotient (@def-difference-quotient),
when that limit exists and is finite.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-left-hand-derivative}
#### Left-hand derivative

Let $f$ be a function defined at $c$.
The **left-hand derivative** of $f$ at $c$ is the left-hand limit (@def-left-hand-limit)
$\lim_{h \to 0^-} \frac{f(c + h) - f(c)}{h}$,
when that limit exists and is finite.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-one-sided-derivative}
#### One-sided derivatives

Let $f$ be a function defined at $c$.
The right-hand derivative (@def-right-hand-derivative) and the left-hand derivative (@def-left-hand-derivative) of $f$ at $c$
are the **one-sided derivatives** of $f$ at $c$.

:::
